titleText.es: Hay que preparar a los niños para esta peculiar explicación; es muy común y está completamente equivocada. Buenas frases son
titleText.en: This is a fun explanation to prepare your kids for; it's common and totally wrong. Good lines include 'why does the air have to travel on both sides at the same time?' and 'I saw the Wright brothers plane and those wings were curved the same on the top and bottom!'
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish source manifest ends after “Buenas frases son ” because the archive page places unescaped quotation marks inside its HTML title attribute. The raw HTML continues with intended Spanish versions of the two quoted examples in the complete official title text. The manifest-truncated Spanish value and the complete official English title text are preserved exactly. OCR also interleaved every panel, split true line-wrapped words, split SUSTENTACIÓN into SUS and TENTACIÓN, read VA as YA, and omitted the accents in PRESIÓN and REVÉS. The visibly duplicated DE DE is a source typo and is transcribed as two lexical occurrences.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Besides meaning “to drive” in much of Latin America, manejar can mean managing or dealing with a person, problem, or situation.

example.en: She knows how to handle difficult situations.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Desafía is a present-time form of desafiar for one person or thing.

example.es: La nueva prueba desafía esa teoría.
example.en: The new evidence challenges that theory.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Perspicaz has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; this de is an accidental duplicate
cardDefinitions.noteEn: An accidental written repetition of de does not add meaning: one copy is redundant. This kind of editing error should be removed in normal Spanish.

example.es: El borrador decía «de de Madrid»; debe decir «de Madrid».
example.en: The draft said ‘de de Madrid’; it should say ‘de Madrid.’

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; links a noun to arriba, ‘above’ or ‘upper’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: De arriba can identify the person or thing located above another reference point. Natural English may use “above,” “upstairs,” or put “upper” before the noun.

example.es: La ventana de arriba está abierta.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: As a judgment on an answer, choice, or response, bien can label it as correct. This differs from bien meaning “well” or opening a reply as “all right.”
Va is the present-time form of ir for one person or thing.
Menor compares an amount, size, or degree. It has the same singular form with masculine and feminine nouns.

example.es: Esta opción tiene un coste menor.
example.en: This option has a lower cost.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Ala is feminine, but singular el is used immediately before it because the word begins with a stressed a sound: el ala. The plural is las alas.
In aviation, sustentación is the upward aerodynamic force that helps support an aircraft.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: no separate English word; begins del revés, ‘upside down’ or ‘inside out’
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Del is the contraction of de + el, but in del revés the two words function together as a fixed orientation expression.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: upside down; inside out (as part of del revés)
cardDefinitions.noteEn: In del revés, revés marks an inverted or reversed orientation.

example.en: You are wearing your T-shirt inside out.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Simplificada is the completed-action form of simplificar used as a description. Its -a ending matches a feminine singular noun.
Equivocada describes a feminine singular person or thing as mistaken or incorrect.

Capitalized Los Reyes commonly refers to the Three Kings, or Magi. In Spain and other Spanish-speaking traditions, children may receive gifts from them around 6 January; their gift-bringing role is culturally comparable to Santa Claus.

example.es: Los Reyes traen regalos en enero.
example.en: The Three Kings bring gifts in January.

cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that something is upside down, inside out, or the wrong way around?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Use del revés after the thing or action whose orientation is reversed.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Del revés is a fixed expression. Its natural English wording depends on the object: a picture may be “upside down,” clothing may be “inside out,” and an ordered sequence may be “backward.”

cardDefinitions.questionEn: Where do common judgment words such as bueno or malo often go?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put them before the noun when they give an overall evaluation: buena idea, mala noticia.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Spanish often puts a neutral descriptive word after its noun, but common evaluation words can come before it. The describing word still changes to match the noun: bueno becomes buena before a feminine singular noun.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: más + palabra que describe cómo se hace algo
cardDefinitions.questionEn: How do you say that an action is done faster, more slowly, or more carefully?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: Put más before the word that describes how the action is done.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Más raises the degree of a manner word. Spanish can use an unchanged form such as rápido or despacio, or an adverb ending in -mente. The other side of the comparison does not have to be stated.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: distancia mayor · aire más rápido · presión menor · del revés
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why does the upside-down-flight question expose a problem with this explanation of lift?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: The explanation assumes that air split by a wing must reunite at the trailing edge at the same time, but air has no such equal-transit-time requirement.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Different airflow speeds and pressures do matter for lift, but the common story that air over the longer curved surface must hurry to meet the air below is false. Lift depends on the complete flow around the wing, including its shape, circulation, and angle of attack. Aircraft can produce lift while inverted by using an appropriate angle of attack, so upside-down flight is a useful counterexample to the oversimplified story.

applications.explanationEn: CÓMO introduces the type of action being explained, and MANEJAR stays in its unchanged dictionary form.
A marks the person directly affected by MANEJAR, and UN ESTUDIANTE completes that person phrase.
ESTUDIANTE names the person, QUE opens the added description, and DESAFÍA TU EXPERIENCIA supplies the information about that person.
PERSPICAZ describes the feminine singular noun PREGUNTA; this adjective keeps the same singular form for either gender.
The neutral descriptive adjective PERSPICAZ follows the noun PREGUNTA.

applications.explanationEn: MAYOR describes the feminine singular noun DISTANCIA and uses its gender-invariant singular form.
The descriptive comparison MAYOR follows DISTANCIA in neutral noun-plus-description order.
POR LO QUE introduces the consequence of the preceding comparison.
TIENE changes for the singular subject, QUE links the construction, and IR remains in dictionary form.
RÁPIDO describes how the movement IR happens; MÁS increases its degree.
MÁS raises the degree of the manner word RÁPIDO.
AIRE names the thing being described, QUE opens the added information, and VA MÁS RÁPIDO states what that air does.
RÁPIDO describes how VA happens and stays in its unchanged masculine singular form.
MÁS raises the degree of RÁPIDO without stating the other side of the comparison.
MENOR describes the feminine singular noun PRESIÓN and keeps its gender-invariant singular form.
The descriptive comparison MENOR follows the noun PRESIÓN.
This second POR LO QUE likewise introduces a claimed consequence.
ALA remains feminine, but its opening stressed a sound makes singular EL the article immediately before it.
